chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hanan ibn Sadir said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say about a man who performed Tawaf but was uncertain (made a mistake)?' He said, 'I said: I performed four (circuits), and he said: I performed three.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'Which of the two Tawafs was it? A Tawaf of a voluntary prayer or a Tawaf of an obligatory duty?' Then he said, 'If it was a Tawaf of an obligatory duty, let him discard what is in his hands (i.e., the circuits he is unsure about) and start anew. And if it was a Tawaf of a voluntary prayer, and he is certain of the three, but is in doubt regarding the fourth whether he performed it or not, let him build upon the third, for it is permissible for him.'.
And whoever performed eight circuits as the Tawaf of the obligatory duty, then it is obligatory upon him to repeat the Tawaf. He narrated that.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person is unsure whether they completed three or four circuits during Hajj Tawaf?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a nuanced legal distinction based on the pilgrim's prior intention, ruling that doubt in obligatory Tawaf requires restarting from scratch to ensure validity, whereas doubt in voluntary Tawaf allows one to build upon the certain count. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of 'presumption of continuity' (istishab) applied to acts of worship, ensuring that uncertainty does not invalidate the core obligation while maintaining rigor for the Fard. The narration also clarifies that performing extra circuits in an obligatory Tawaf does not invalidate it but requires the pilgrim to account for the additional rounds, highlighting the flexibility within strict ritual frameworks.
